## Loading R package

### Installing **catchment** R package from github

Use the code chunk below to install catchment R package from github.

```{r}
remotes::install_github('uva-bi-sdad/catchment')
```

Next, load sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility and catchment R packages into RStudio environment using the code chunk below

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility, catchment) 
```

## Importing geospatial data

Use the code chunk below to import the three geospatial data: MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL, hexagons and ELDERCARE

```{r}
#| output: false
mpsz <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
#| output: false
hexagons <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                    layer = "hexagons") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
#| output: false
eldercare <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial", 
                     layer = "ELDERCARE") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

Next, use the code chunk below to import OD_Matrix.csv into RStudio environment.

```{r}
#| output: false
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
```

## Geospatial Preparation

Use the code chunk below to create a new field called *capacity* in *eldercare* sf data frame and populate **100** in it.

```{r}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
```

Use the code chunk below to create a new field called *demand* in *hexagons* sf data frame and populate value **100** in it.

```{r}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)
```

Use the code chunk the select origin_id, destination_id and total_cost from ODMatrix data frame. Then, rename them to from_id, to_id and dist respectively.

```{r}
ODMatrix_tidied <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  rename(from_id = origin_id,
         to_id = destination_id,
         dist = total_cost)
```

## Computing Minimum Travel Distace to nearest oldercare

In the code chunk below, `cost_to_closest()` of **accessibility** package is used to calculates the minimum travel distance to the closest n number (i.e. n=1) of opportunities.

```{r}
dist2closest <- cost_to_closest(
  travel_matrix = ODMatrix_tidied,
  land_use_data = hexagons,
  opportunity = "demand",
  travel_cost = "dist",
  n = 1,
  group_by = character(0),
  active = TRUE,
  fill_missing_ids = TRUE
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Joining output

Use the code chunk below to append the computed closest distance values to *hexagons* sf data frame.

```{r}
hex_acc <- hexagons %>%
  left_join(dist2closest) %>%
  rename(dist2closest = dist)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Mapping closest distance

::: panel-tabset
### The plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
mapex <- st_bbox(hex_acc)
tm_shape(hex_acc,
         bbox = mapex) + 
  tm_polygons(fill = "dist2closest", 
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to the closest eldercare") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

### The code chunk

Code chunk below will be used to prepare a chotolepth map showing the distribution of closest values in *dist* field.

```{r}
#| eval: false
mapex <- st_bbox(hex_acc)
tm_shape(hex_acc,
         bbox = mapex) + 
  tm_polygons(fill = "dist2closest", 
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to the closest eldercare") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +

```
:::

## Converting ODMatrix data frame in a matrix

In the code chunk below as.matrix() is used to convert ODMatrix data frame into a Mamtrix object.

```{r}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost)%>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)
```

## Two-Step Floating Catchment Area

In this code chunk below, `[catchment_ratio()](https://uva-bi-sdad.github.io/catchment/reference/catchment_ratio.html)` of catchment package is used to compute 2SFCA.

```{r}
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand, 
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Mapping 2SFCA

::: panel-tabset
### The plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
hex_2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca) 
tm_shape(hex_2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) + 
  tm_polygons(fill = "2SFCA", 
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("2SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +

```

## Enhanced 2-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)

```{r}
step_weights <- list(c(5, .01), c(4, .05), c(3, .1), c(2, .4), c(1, 1))
df_e2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand, 
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = step_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("E2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Modified 2-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_m2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand, 
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  step_weights, 
  adjust_providers = function(w) w^2) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("M2SFCA" = ".")
```
